original_card.question: Can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk?
methods: Derive a fully charged favorable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision.
Prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show the changed centre charge and copy profile per call with every added restoration or hosting cost charged, and its ceiling via ceiling.ceiling(centre=...).

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the per-call centre charge and copy children for sharing across k = 2 calls, charge the sharing overhead, and screen it; stop this route if even the ideal sharing gains under 10%. Ideal budgets: free 2.80x, shared by two 1.90x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The centre path consumes 64 of about 99.6 unpaid coordinates per call, i.e. about 64% of the raw deficit.
allowed_variations: One sharing pattern across a fixed number of calls.
One reduced copied-total contract for the existing decoder.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Removing copies without a replacement contract for the decoder's copied totals.

actual_scope: Fully charged favorable relaxation of k-call centre sharing on the actual selected #1094 complex and PR589 bit histograms: exact residuals for k = 2..144, sharp integer overhead budgets (extra paid children per rank) keeping the full bit-limited gain or any gain, the minimum complex saving that makes the bit side bind, the bit endpoint and bit-side net saving needed for the card's 10% target, and the scalar-overhead room under the binding finite guard.
scope_change_reason: PR1708/PR1748 already construct the two-call centre phases and PR1708 screened the ideal relaxation (+3.4536% cap); this replaces ideal packing with the actual histograms and prices the open overhead DeltaH and the joint bit-side requirement instead of building another sharing word.
bottleneck_link: Centre sharing alone is capped at +3.4536% because the bit side binds; the card's stop rule (ideal gain under 10%) therefore applies unless a bit-side mechanism nets at least 649 paid-mass units. The DeltaH budget tells implementers how much sharing overhead is affordable. No kappa claim.
stop_rule: Stop after the k-table, the two-call per-rank budgets, the complex-to-bit binding margin, the 10% bit requirement and the scalar guard room are exact; do not construct a sharing word or a bit mechanism.
evidence: RESULT.json: k=2 sharing leaves f(c)-1 = -4.25e-3 at the bit endpoint; DeltaH up to 30.5-30.8 units/call keeps the full +3.4536% (kappa 0.001730427469823602), up to ~32 keeps any gain (break-even control exact at 576 rank-8); complex binds by 1.23-1.33 units/call; +10% needs bit endpoint 0.0018433 (x1.0634) and >= 649 net bit paid-mass units; <= 654,144 extra macros per call under the 2^48 guard. Reused DE-diagnostic enclosure and seed81 formulas unchanged.

open_questions.question: Can a bit-side mechanism net at least 649 paid-mass units (deficit 10,272 -> >= 10,921), so that any complex saving of >= 1.33 units per call (e.g. two-call centre sharing) reaches the card's +10% target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Centre sharing alone is capped at +3.4536% by the bit side; the joint requirement is the only route to the 10% target for this lever.
open_questions.first_step: Price the bit-revision3-levers-seed03 bit levers at endpoint 0.0018433 with this package's sharp-removal method.
open_questions.blocked_by: No bit construction with that saving is known; bit copy-charge and full-frame-helper floors are scoped obstructions.
